newsitem.title: USA: Florida asks judge to restore tobacco defendants.
newsitem.headline: Florida asks judge to restore tobacco defendants.

text.p: Attorneys for the state of Florida on Thursday asked a state appeals court to overrule a lower court decision dismissing B.A.T Industries Plc, Loews Corp and Batus Holdings Inc as defendants in the state's $1 billion Medicaid lawsuit.

The state said it had presented Palm Beach Circuit Court Judge Harold Cohen last September with sufficient evidence to show that the three holding companies controlled the activities of their subsidiaries in Florida.
In September Cohen dismissed the three holding companies as defendants after finding they did not actively operate tobacco businesses.
B.A.T is the parent of Brown and Williamson Tobacco Co, which is run under the umbrella of Batus Holdings Inc, a corporation created by B.A.T.
The state alleges that Loews participates in the manufacture and sale of cigarette and tobacco products through its agent, Lorrillard Tobacco Co.

Edna Caruso, one of Florida's appeal attorneys, told the appellate court that Cohen should have retained the companies as defendants because there was sufficient evidence to support including them in the lawsuit.

Florida attorneys alleged that Batus and Loews were involved in the "industry conspiracy to suppress scientific research to mislead the public and regulatory bodies," so that it could pursue "targeting" of the youth market.

But B.A.T attorney Jane Kreusler Walsh said the company keeps a loose hold on its subsidiaries. "It would have been physically impossible (for B.A.T) to exercise the control alleged by (Florida) with only 185 employees," she said.

Florida is seeking $1 billion in damages, which could be tripled if the state can prove the tobacco companies engaged in criminal conduct in the sale and marketing of cigarettes. The case is set to go to trial August 4.
